title: What If the World's Biggest Lake Dropped 18 Meters?

scenes.text: What if the world's biggest lake dropped 18 meters? The Caspian Sea could.
It has no outlet. Its level depends on rain, rivers and evaporation, and it relies mainly on the Volga.
Right now it is already falling about six to seven centimeters a year.
A nine-meter drop would dry out nearly all of the shallow northern shelf, and part of the Turkmen shelf.
Ports would be left far from the water, and fish, birds and seals would lose spawning grounds and food.
In the worst case, an 18-meter drop shrinks the sea's surface by about 34 percent. Scientists say cutting emissions alone may no longer save it.

description:
What if the world's biggest lake dropped 18 meters?
Studies say the Caspian Sea could fall 9 to 18 meters this century, and it is already dropping about 6 to 7 centimeters a year.
